description: Word-level Bare Act footnotes for Learn Read/Card hover (memorized unit.text stays plain). schema 1.1 adds structured tip content + shared notes for nested refs. schema 1.2 adds optional surfaces ([browse]/[learn]; default both) so diglot footer tips can be Browse-only.

article-55-2026-amendment.note: Subs. by the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001, s. 2, for "2000" (w.e.f. 21-2-2002).

article-54.note: "State" includes the National Capital Territory of Delhi and the Union territory of *Puducherry.

article-124-clause-1.note: Now “thirty-three” vide the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 (37 of 2019), s. 2 (w.e.f. 9-8-2019).

article-326.note: Subs. by the Constitution (Sixty-first Amendment) Act, 1988, s. 2, for "twenty-one years" (w.e.f. 28-3-1989).

content.value: In this article, the expression "population" means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published: Provided that the reference in this Explanation to the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published shall, until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year
have been published, be construed as a reference to the 1971 census.

article-21a.note: Ins. by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, s. 2 (w.e.f. 1-4-2010).

article-32a.note: Art. 32A omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, s. 3 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978).

article-38-clause-2.note: Ins. by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 9 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979).

article-39a.note: Ins. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 8 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

article-48a.note: Ins. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 10 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

article-51a.note: Part IVA / Art. 51A ins. by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 11 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977).

article-51a-subclause-k.note: Ins. by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, s. 4 (w.e.f. 1-4-2010).

article-77-clause-3.note: Cl. (4) was inserted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 14 (w.e.f. 3-1-1977) and omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 12 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979).

article-87-clause-1.note: Subs. by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, s. 7, for "every session" (w.e.f. 18-6-1951).

article-87-clause-2.note: The words "and for the precedence of such discussion over other business of the House" omitted by the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, s. 7 (w.e.f. 18-6-1951).

article-102-clause-1.note: Subs. by the Constitution (Fifty-second Amendment) Act, 1985, s. 3, for "(2) for the purposes of this art." (w.e.f. 1-3-1985).

article-170-clause-3.note: Art. 170’s composition and readjustment clauses include diglot insertions on census-based delimitation and the freeze until the first census taken after the year 2026. Browse keeps the Bare Act wording used for learning.

article-128.note: After the Ninety-ninth Amendment (NJAC) was struck down, art. 128 again lets the Chief Justice of India (with the President’s previous consent) request a retired Supreme Court or High Court Judge to sit and act as a Supreme Court Judge.

article-123-clause-3.note: Cl. (4) of art. 123 was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 16 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). The Bare Act keeps cls. (1)–(3) and the Explanation only.

article-144a.note: Art. 144A (special provision as to disposal of questions relating to constitutional validity of laws) was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-third Amendment) Act, 1977, s. 5 (w.e.f. 13-4-1978). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-166-clause-3.note: Cl. (4) of art. 166 was omitted (diglot markings / Forty-second Amendment history). The Bare Act keeps cls. (1)–(3) only.

article-132-clause-3.note: Cl. (2) of art. 132 was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 17 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). The Bare Act keeps cls. (1) and (3) plus the Explanation.

article-189-clause-3.note: Art. 189’s diglot brackets and omission markers around voting and quorum wording are stripped in the Bare Act restore so cls. (1)–(4) read as continuous operative text.

article-151-clause-2.note: In cl. (2), the words “or Rajpramukh” were omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. The Bare Act now refers only to the Governor of a State.

article-192-clause-1.note: Art. 192 (decision on questions as to disqualifications of members) is a separate Bare Act article from art. 191. Diglot/PDF glue had merged its text into 191; this restore keeps Governor / Election Commission wording under art. 192 only.

article-127-clause-1.note: After the Ninety-ninth Amendment (NJAC) was struck down, art. 127 again requires the Chief Justice of India to be consulted / to request attendance of an ad hoc Judge (not the National Judicial Appointments Commission).

article-176-clause-1.note: Art. 176’s diglot markings record later wording for the Governor’s special address at the commencement of the first session each year. The Bare Act text used here omits the struck/superseded fragments.

article-153.note: The proviso allowing one person to be appointed Governor for two or more States was inserted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 6.

article-124c.note: Art. 124C (Parliament’s power to regulate NJAC procedure) was inserted by the Constitution (Ninety-ninth Amendment) Act, 2014 and later omitted after that Amendment was struck down. The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-124b.note: Art. 124B (functions of the National Judicial Appointments Commission) was inserted by the Constitution (Ninety-ninth Amendment) Act, 2014 and later omitted after that Amendment was struck down. The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-49.target: declared by or under law made by Parliament
article-49.note: Subs. by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 27, for "declared by Parliament by law" (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

article-208-clause-3.note: The brackets and words “(including the quorum to constitute a meeting of the House)” were inserted by the Forty-second Amendment and later omitted by the Forty-fourth Amendment. The Bare Act keeps clause (3) without that diglot footer.

article-210-clause-2.note: Diglot insertions substitute “twenty-five years” / “forty years” for particular State Legislatures (Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Tripura; Arunachal Pradesh, Goa and Mizoram). Browse keeps the operative Bare Act provisos.

article-216.note: The proviso to article 216 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 11 (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

article-217-clause-1.note: After the Ninety-ninth Amendment (NJAC) was struck down, article 217 again requires appointment after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State, and (except for the Chief Justice) the Chief Justice of the High Court.

article-219.note: The words “in a State” were omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-11-1956).

article-221-clause-1.note: Clause (1) was substituted by the Constitution (Fifty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1986, s. 3; diglot brackets around the substituted wording are stripped in the Bare Act restore.

article-222-clause-1.note: After the Ninety-ninth Amendment (NJAC) was struck down, article 222(1) again lets the President transfer a Judge after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.

article-224a.target: Chief Justice of a High Court
article-224a.note: After the Ninety-ninth Amendment (NJAC) was struck down, article 224A again lets the Chief Justice of a High Court (with the President’s previous consent) request a retired Judge to sit and act as a Judge of that High Court.

article-242.note: Article 242 (Coorg) was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-244-clause-1.note: State-name diglot insertions (Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram) record later amendments to the Fifth/Sixth Schedule carve-out. Browse keeps the Bare Act State list.

article-246-clause-1.note: Diglot asterisks/brackets around “also” / “in a State” wording are stripped so clauses (1)–(4) read as continuous Bare Act text.

article-248-clause-1.note: Ins. by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, s. 3 (w.e.f. 16-9-2016).

article-249-clause-1.target: goods and services tax provided under article 246A or
article-249-clause-1.note: Ins. by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, s. 4 (w.e.f. 16-9-2016).

article-250-clause-1.target: goods and services tax provided under article 246A or
article-250-clause-1.note: Ins. by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, s. 5 (w.e.f. 16-9-2016).

article-254-clause-2.note: Diglot asterisks after “Legislature of a State” were omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956. The Bare Act restore keeps the proviso under clause (2).

article-255.note: Diglot asterisks after “Legislature of a State” were omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch.

article-257a.note: Article 257A was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 33 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-259.note: Article 259 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-288-clause-1.target: law of a State in force
article-288-clause-1.note: Explanation.—The expression 'law of a State in force' in this clause shall include a law of a State passed or made before the commencement of this Constitution and not previously repealed, notwithstanding that it or parts of it may not be then in operation either at all or in particular areas.

article-264.note: The diglot Bare Act closes article 264 with a trailing amendment bracket (']'). This app prints the operative definition without that marker.

article-267-clause-2.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-268-clause-1.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted excise-on-medicinal-and-toilet-preparations wording as '2***' after 'stamp duties'. This app prints the current Bare Act without that marker.

article-268a.note: Article 268A was omitted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, s. 7 (w.e.f. 16-9-2016). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-269-clause-1.note: Article 269A (GST on inter-State supplies) was inserted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016. Diglot amendment brackets around clause (1) are stripped in this app.

article-271.target: except the goods and services tax under article 246A
article-271.note: The GST carve-out was inserted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016. Diglot brackets are stripped; article 272’s omission note is not glued here.

article-272.note: Article 272 was omitted by the Constitution (Eightieth Amendment) Act, 2000, s. 4 (w.e.f. 9-6-2000). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-278.note: Article 278 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. (w.e.f. 1-11-1956). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-283-clause-2.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-286-clause-1.target: supply of goods or of services or both
article-286-clause-1.note: Substituted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, for the earlier “sale or purchase of goods” formulation. Diglot superscripts are stripped.

article-290a.note: Article 290A was inserted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 19; “Tamil Nadu” substituted for “Madras” by the Madras State (Alteration of Name) Act, 1968.

article-291.note: Article 291 was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1971, s. 2. The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-299-clause-1.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-300a.note: Article 300A was inserted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 34. The diglot trailing “]” is stripped.

article-304.note: Inserted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. Diglot brackets/superscripts are stripped; the operative words remain.

article-306.note: Article 306 was omitted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-308.note: The diglot Bare Act marks the J&K carve-out with amendment brackets ('1 […]'). This app keeps the operative Bare Act wording without those markers.

article-309.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 2 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-310-clause-2.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 2 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-311-clause-2.note: Clauses (2) and (3) were substituted by the Constitution (Fifteenth Amendment) Act, 1963, and further amended by the Forty-second Amendment. Diglot markers and trailing “]” debris are stripped.

article-312-clause-1.target: Chapter VI of Part VI or Part XI
article-312-clause-1.note: Substituted/inserted language from the Forty-second Amendment (all-India judicial service). Diglot brackets are stripped; article 312A is not glued after clause (4).

article-314.note: Article 314 was omitted by the Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972, s. 3 (w.e.f. 29-8-1972). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-315-clause-4.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-269a-clause-1.note: Article 269A was inserted by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, s. 9 (w.e.f. 16-9-2016).

article-312a-clause-1.note: Article 312A was inserted by the Constitution (Twenty-eighth Amendment) Act, 1972, s. 2 (w.e.f. 29-8-1972).

article-323-clause-2.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***' / 'Governor 2 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-330-clause-2.note:
Explanation.—In this article and in article 332, the expression 'population' means the population as ascertained at the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published:

Provided that the reference in this Explanation to the last preceding census of which the relevant figures have been published shall, until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, be construed as a reference to the 2001 census.
Inserted by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956, s. 29 and Sch. Diglot brackets/superscripts are stripped; the operative words remain.

article-320-clause-3.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 1 ***' / '2 ***'. This app prints 'Governor' only.

article-329.note: The diglot Bare Act marked a Thirty-ninth / Forty-fourth Amendment wrapper and omitted 'but subject to the provisions of article 329A' as '2 ***'. This app prints the operative Bare Act stem without those markers.

article-329a.note: Article 329A was omitted by the Constitution (Forty-fourth Amendment) Act, 1978, s. 36 (w.e.f. 20-6-1979). The Bare Act prints “[Omitted.]”.

article-332-clause-1.target: except the Scheduled Tribes in the autonomous districts of Assam
article-332-clause-1.note: Substituted by the Constitution (Fifty-first Amendment) Act, 1984. Diglot brackets and omitted Part A/B Schedule wording (`3 ***`) are stripped.

article-333.note: The diglot Bare Act shows omitted Rajpramukh wording as 'Governor 2 ***' and marks the nomination phrase with amendment brackets. This app prints the operative Bare Act wording without those markers.

article-368-clause-3.note: Cls. (4) and (5) were inserted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976, s. 55, and declared invalid by the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India, AIR 1980 SC 1789. They are omitted from the memorized Bare Act text.
